look_here_first: Start with mature acorn shape plus the scaly cup: Texas live oak often has a narrow, noticeably pointed/spindle-like nut ~20–30 mm long seated in a relatively deep funnel/goblet cup. Combine this with pale appressed-stellate leaf undersides and central Texas limestone habitat; leaf shape or evergreen habit alone is insufficient.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Tree or shrub; often subevergreen; shrubby plants may form large clonal stands.

key_traits.label: Bark
key_traits.text: Dark brown to black and scaly.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Oblong-elliptic to narrowly ovate/lanceolate; margins entire or with a few teeth and often minutely revolute; lower surface pale/whitish from dense appressed stellate hairs.

key_traits.label: Acorn
key_traits.text: Nut dark brown, often longitudinally striped, subfusiform and acute to narrowly barrel-shaped; cup funnel-, hemispheric-, or deeply goblet-shaped.
